title: Client retry ecosystem: SLO-driven hedge protocol and idempotency handshake
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define and implement a standardized client-side retry and hedging protocol across Redwood SDKs and runtime bindings that is driven by service SLOs, preserves safe semantics via an idempotency handshake, and interoperates with runtime circuit breakers and load-shedding policies. This ticket scopes the API surface, runtime expectations, rollout strategy, and observability required for an enterprise-compatible migration.
background: We currently have divergent retry/backoff behaviors across language SDKs and service clients: some SDKs do fixed exponential backoff, others do simple retry-with-deadline, and hedging support exists in a few services only. This variance causes unpredictable client-side load amplification during partial regional outages and complicates cross-service SLO guarantees. Additionally, idempotency key usage is inconsistent, resulting in duplicate-side effects for non-idempotent endpoints. Runtime circuit breakers and load-shedding sometimes react too late because client retries silently increase concurrency.
proposal: Introduce a pluggable "SLO-driven Retry Ecosystem" consisting of: 1) a compact cross-SDK header + handshake for idempotency metadata (Idempotency-Key, Idempotency-Alg, Idempotency-Proto-Version), 2) a standardized retry policy specification (per-route retry budget, max attempts, base and jittered backoffs, hedging window), 3) client-side SLO mapping that converts service SLOs into local retry/hedge decisions, 4) explicit signals to runtime circuit breakers and load-shedders (Retry-Intent, Hedge-Group) so the runtime can account for safe retries and apply quota-aware shedding, and 5) telemetry contracts for retry/hedge observability. The system must be opt-in per route initially and backward-compatible: default behavior remains "no aggressive hedging" until SDK upgrade and server-side opt-in.
api_changes: - New request headers: Idempotency-Key (UUIDv4 or user-provided), Idempotency-Alg (e.g., "simple-v1"), Idempotency-Proto-Version: 1. - Retry-Control header to carry client-selected policy hints (e.g., "budget=20;max_attempts=3;base_ms=50;max_ms=2000;hedge_ms=75"). - Response headers for server feedback: Retry-Allowed (yes|no|conditional), Preferred-Retry-Policy. - SDK will expose a RetryPolicy object with fields: maxAttempts, perAttemptDeadlineMs, baseBackoffMs, maxBackoffMs, jitter, hedgeWindowMs, budgetKey (route-level). - Backwards-compatible: if Retry-Control not present or server replies Retry-Allowed=no, SDK falls back to previous behavior.
sdk_changes: - Update JS, Python, Go, Java SDKs to include built-in RetryPolicy and Idempotency helpers. - Provide an IdempotencyKey class that generates RFC-compliant keys and exposes optional deterministic keys for user-provided dedup. - Default SDK behavior: map route SLO hints to a conservative policy (maxAttempts=2, hedgeWindowMs=0) unless route is explicitly labeled "hedge-safe" in service metadata. - Add opt-in config: client.retry.strategy = 'slo-driven' | 'legacy' | 'none'. - Add helper: WithIdempotency(key) wrapper for mutable operations. - Provide shim so older SDKs gracefully ignore new headers.
runtime_changes: - Runtime will understand Retry-Intent and Hedge-Group headers and account for hedged requests in admission control and autoscaling signals. - Circuit breaker integration: introduce a new internal metric "inflight_safe_retries" and make circuit-breaker thresholds configurable to include/exclude hedged attempts. - Load-shedding policies must support conditional shedding when Retry-Allowed=no. - Region-aware failover: when a region reports degraded SLO (observability signal > threshold), client SLO mapping increases hedgeWindowMs only if server advertises hedge-safe. - Provide a runtime API for feature flags: route is_hedge_safe, recommended_retry_policy.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (4 weeks): Spec and SDK prototypes, add header parsing in runtime as a no-op (log-only) to gather telemetry. Phase 2 (6 weeks): Implement full SDK behaviors and runtime accounting behind a feature flag; run canary with internal services labeled hedge-safe. Phase 3 (8 weeks): Expand opt-in to customer-facing routes, add canary traffic for multi-region failover scenarios. Phase 4 (ongoing): Gradual default flip for routes that meet safety checks and have strong monitoring. Rollback plan: SDKs can be downgraded and runtime feature-flag can be turned off; record a rollback checklist in runbook.
rollout: - Week 1-2: Developer previews for internal teams; gather integration feedback. - Week 3-6: Canary in prod for control plane and a small subset of CPU-bound inference endpoints. - Week 7-12: Opt-in expansion to Dedicated customers with explicit contract and support. - Post rollout: three-month monitoring window for regressions with automated alerts on duplicate writes, idempotency_conflicts > 0.1% per 10k requests, and unexpected latency amplification.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Required metrics and dashboards: - client.retry.attempts (counter, labels: route, region, SDK-lang) - client.hedged.attempts (counter) - idempotency.conflicts (counter) - retry.backoff.distribution (histogram) - route.retry_budget_utilization (gauge) - shed.rate_by_route (gauge) - p99_latency_with_and_without_retries (histogram)
  Alerts: - idempotency.conflicts > 0.001 * requests over 5m => page on-call, tag owner. - rate_of_inflight_hedges causing queue_growth > 10% => trigger mitigation (reduce hedging). - retry_budget_utilization > 90% for 10m => review route policy.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs produce Idempotency-Key and Retry-Control headers per spec and are backward-compatible
Runtime correctly records hedged attempts and exposes retry budget metrics
No increase in duplicate side-effects after canary (idempotency_conflicts remains <= baseline + 0.0005)
Circuit breaker thresholds respect hedged attempt accounting and do not cause oscillation in steady state
Successful multi-region failover test: client hedge protocol reduces tail latency without amplifying overall QPS beyond configured budget
risks: Clients could misconfigure idempotency keys leading to accidental deduplication or missed retries
Uncontrolled hedging can amplify load during wide-scale outages if runtime accounting is imperfect
Complexity across SDKs increases maintenance burden and risk of inconsistent behavior
Late discovery of incompatible third-party clients that ignore new headers could create asymmetric failure modes
open_questions: What is the canonical idempotency key TTL on the server side (24h vs 7d)?
How should we encode multi-request transactions that are not single-operation idempotent?
Do we want a central service that suggests per-route retry budgets or allow teams to configure locally?
How to version the Idempotency-Alg safely to support future dedup strategies (hashing+payload-fingerprint)?
